evidence.exact_quote: Canonical `wake_reason` is closed to `prerequisite_resolved | approval_resolved | clarification_resolved | auth_recovered | startup_recovered | backoff_expired | verification_completed | remediation_resolved | safe_point_restored | capacity_available | replan_applied | watchdog_recheck`. `startup_recovered` is the scheduler-pass value used for the first pass after startup recovery, while `watchdog_recheck` is a defensive verification wake that may recheck readiness without becoming the primary correctness path.

`filesafe.policy_degraded` is valid only when enforcement remains fail-closed or an embedded fallback baseline remains authoritative enough to block known destructive operations. It must not stand in for missing/empty allowlists, missing roots, unresolved canonical paths, failed guard initialization, or destructive override denial.

items.impact: Implementers have a canonical event, recovery, blocked-state, and fail-closed safety vocabulary instead of relying on UI prose or legacy aliases.
items.statement: The window establishes canonical scheduler, blocked/unblocked, retry, safe-point, FileSafe denial, remediation, degradation, wizard, attempt, timeout, and recovery contracts with explicit aliases and fail-closed boundaries.
items.title: Canonical runtime event and recovery contract family

evidence.exact_quote: - `restore_outcome`

For a worktree-bound attempt, `safe_point.created` MUST capture the exact worktree snapshot fields `worktree_id`, `worktree_path`, `branch_name`, and `HEAD_sha`. Restore and retry flows verify the captured worktree context and expected `HEAD_sha` before mutation-capable work continues; if the worktree path, branch name, or HEAD state no longer matches, the recovery flow reports a blocked/stale baseline rather than silently substituting the main project root or a different worktree.

items.impact: Different builders could report the same restore outcome while omitting which worktree/branch/HEAD comparison was performed, weakening replay, stale-baseline diagnosis, and mutation admission proofs.
items.statement: The text mandates exact worktree-context verification before mutation but the `safe_point.restored` minimum payload does not require the observed worktree, branch, expected/actual HEAD, verification result, or blocked-event reference that proves the check occurred.
items.title: Safe-point restore verification is not receipt-complete
